subject: MAP: Performance benchmark scoping — latency, concurrency & TTFT roadmap

- A clear workload definition that mirrors our production mix (message length, avg tokens per request, ratio of short vs long inferences).
- Success criteria (TTFT, p95/p99 latency, throughput per GPU, sustained concurrency).
- A short test plan and timeline that gets us to a sign-off before the end of November.

For context: our pilot target is to mimic peak marketing events: ~12k concurrent web sessions at peak, average prompt length ~80 tokens, generation length ~150 tokens. We can provide sample request traces if helpful (attached a small telemetry sample).

Alex —

Appreciate the context and the telemetry sample. I pulled together a compact benchmarking scope that will live inside the MAP and map to the procurement acceptance gates. Key points below; attached is a draft MAP scope spreadsheet and an initial Redwood benchmark config you can review.

Proposed MAP benchmarking scoping (high level):

1) Workload definition
   - Mix: 65% short (<=60 tokens total), 30% medium (61-200 tokens), 5% long (>200 tokens).
   - Traffic profile: baseline steady of 100 qps, daily peaks up to 600 qps, simulated marketing spikes of 1,200 qps for 2–5 minutes.
   - Input distribution: include 10% multi-turn chat sessions to exercise KV cache behavior.

2) Success criteria (pass/fail gates)
   - Time-to-first-token (TTFT): p95 <= 350 ms; p99 <= 700 ms.
   - Latency (generation end-to-end): p95 <= 1.2s for medium prompts; p95 <= 2.5s for long prompts.
   - Throughput: sustain 8 tokens/sec per GPU on average (quantized runtime); measured over 10-minute steady window.
   - Concurrency resilience: maintain SLOs while autoscaling from baseline to target burst within 60s.

3) Test phases and cadence
   - Phase A (baseline): single instance / small pool, sanity checks, warm cache runs — 2 days.
   - Phase B (production-like sustained): 4 hours steady runs at target qps to measure throughput and costs — 1 day.
   - Phase C (spike & recovery): 3x short-duration spike tests to validate autoscaling and fallback behavior — 1 day.
   - Phase D (regression): final acceptance run with customer workload trace — 1 day.

4) Data & artifacts
   - We will produce a result summary with token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latency tables, TTFT distribution, and traces (console link).

Next steps I propose: Karthik will propose the exact load profiles and harness; Marissa will own the acceptance doc and sign-off checklist. Can we target the MAP to be finalized by midday 18 Nov so procurement has time to process? I attached: datawave-map-scope-v1.xlsx and redwood-benchmark-config.json for your review.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Soojin — adding the infra/testing perspective. Below are concrete test definitions and pass/fail thresholds we will run in the Redwood harness (we use a combination of synthetic load and replayed traces). Quoted the proposed scoping above for reference.

> Traffic profile: baseline steady of 100 qps, daily peaks up to 600 qps, simulated marketing spikes of 1,200 qps for 2–5 minutes.

Proposed technical plan (details):

- Test harness:
  - Locust-based driver for request-level replay; token-level measurement instrumented inside our runtime.
  - Two modes: replay (exact trace) and synthetic (parameterized).

- Key measurements:
  - TTFT definition: time from request accept to first token emitted; measured at p50/p95/p99.
  - End-to-end generation latency: includes model compute + network + streaming headroom.
  - Per-GPU throughput: tokens/sec as observed at runtime.

- Load profiles (runs):
  1) Warmup: 15 minutes at 20% target to heat KV caches.
  2) Steady-state run: 10 minutes at target qps (100, 300, 600) — report mean & percentiles. Repeat x3.
  3) Spike test: ramp to 1,200 qps over 30s, hold 3 minutes, drop to baseline; repeat 3 times.
  4) Long-run stability: 1 hour at 300 qps to check memory growth and tail latencies.

- Acceptance thresholds (engineered):
  - TTFT p95 <= 350 ms (green), p95 350–500 ms (amber), >500 ms (red).
  - Generation p95 <= thresholds Soojin listed (1.2s medium, 2.5s long).
  - No more than 2% of requests should experience streaming interruption/fallback.
  - Autoscaling: system must return to baseline within 90s after spike end with <5% request error rate.

- Reporting artifacts we will hand off:
  - CSV of per-request latencies and token counts, condensed dashboard screenshots, and a short run-book of how to reproduce tests in your environment.

I will schedule the harness runs on Redwood Dedicated staging on 17 Nov 2026 (we need your confirmation on the final trace file). If anything here looks off, flag it and we can tighten the windows.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
